h1: The 8 Best Robot Vacuums for Large Homes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Large-Home Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot vacuums for large homes, scored on runtime, self-empty interval and mopping, from roborock to eufy and ILIFE.
summary: The roborock Q7 M5+ is the one to buy for a big house: 10,000Pa suction and a dock rated for up to 7 to 9 weeks of debris. For the strongest raw suction, the eufy E25 goes to 20,000Pa. If you want long stretches between emptying on less money, the MONSGA is the budget answer. And for a tight budget, the ILIFE A30 Pro keeps 10,000Pa under $200.
intro: A robot vacuum that is fine in a two-bedroom flat can quietly fail in a big house. The failure is rarely suction. It is that the battery dies halfway through the downstairs, the dustbin fills before the hallway is done, and you end up carrying it back to a dock yourself.

So this ranking leans on the specs that matter at scale: stated runtime per charge, how long the dock goes before you must empty it, and whether it can mop as well as vacuum. We reviewed eight current models from established and newer brands, scored them on the Primea framework, and weighted endurance above headline Pa numbers.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: 10,000Pa suction and the longest self-empty interval here. Built for a house that makes a lot of dust.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ pairs 10,000Pa suction with a self-empty dock rated for up to 7 to 9 weeks of debris. In a large home that is the spec that decides whether the robot feels automatic or becomes another chore, because a full bin is what stops most machines mid-job.

It takes the top spot over the eufy E25 despite lower suction because endurance and routine matter more across many rooms. roborock's mapping platform is mature, which generally means steadier room-by-room routes than newer entrants. You give up the extreme Pa rating of the eufy and the roller-mop cleaning system, and you get a simpler, calmer machine.

Choose it if you want a robot you can forget about for weeks at a time and your floors are a mix of hard surface and low carpet.
pros: Vacuums and mops in one run
products.idealFor: Large homes that want weeks between manual dock emptying.
products.skipIf: You need top-tier suction for deep, ground-in dirt.

products.name: eufy E25 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: 20,000Pa and a HydroJet roller mop. The deep-clean option for homes with heavy dirt.
products.description:
The E25 posts the highest suction in this guide at 20,000Pa and pairs it with a HydroJet roller mop. A roller mop is cleaned as it works, so the pad is not dragged across the floor getting dirtier with every room, which matters when there are many rooms.

It ranks just under the roborock because suction is only half of a large-home story. The roborock advertises the longer hands-off dock interval, while the eufy is the pick when floor type and dirt load are the bigger challenge. It also sits at the premium end of the group.

Best for homes with pets, kids or a lot of hard flooring, where the mop quality and raw pickup matter more than saving a little on the dock.
pros: Roller mop cleans itself in use
cons: Dock interval not the longest here
products.idealFor: Pet households and hard-floor homes with heavy dirt.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest way to cover a big floor plan.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo
products.verdict: One dock empties the bin and washes the mop pads. Separate hardwood and carpet modes.
products.description:
The Omni C20 relies on eufy's single station, which empties the dustbin and washes the mop pads. That second job is what most basic docks skip, and it means the mop does not need manual rinsing after every large-home run.

Compared with the E25 above, it gives up the 20,000Pa headline number but keeps the dock convenience in a more practical package. Dedicated hardwood and carpet modes let it change its behavior as it moves between rooms, which suits a house with mixed flooring.

Pick it if your home mixes hardwood with carpet and you want washing and emptying handled by one station.
pros: Dock empties bin and washes pads
cons: Bigger dock needs more floor space
products.idealFor: Mixed hardwood and carpet homes that want a hands-off mop.
products.skipIf: You have little room for a large docking station.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: 10,000Pa on roborock's proven navigation. A steady choice for houses with shedding pets.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ brings 10,000Pa suction to roborock's navigation platform, plus a self-emptying S5+ dock. Pet hair is a volume problem, and a large house produces a lot of it, so a bin that empties itself matters as much as the suction.

It sits below the Q7 M5+ because the Q7 spells out a longer dock interval, which is the clearer advantage in a big home. The two share the same brand strengths and the same suction rating, so the choice is mainly about which dock and feature set suits your house.

Good for buyers who like roborock's route planning and want a reliable pet hair machine without chasing the biggest Pa figure.
cons: Dock interval less clearly stated than Q7
products.idealFor: Houses with shedding pets and several rooms to map.
products.skipIf: Maximum dock interval is your top priority.

products.name: MONSGA Robot Vacuum and Mop, 90 Days Self-Emptying
products.verdict: A 90-day dock and 8000Pa at a lower price than the big brands. The budget way to go hands-off.
products.description:
MONSGA advertises a 90-day self-emptying interval from its large-capacity base, which closely matches the roborock Q7 M5+ at the top of this list. Add 8000Pa suction and mopping, and it targets the same goal of going long stretches without touching the machine.

It ranks fifth because the brand has a shorter track record and less ecosystem depth than roborock or eufy. The tradeoff is simple: you save money and get the same headline dock promise, but you accept a less established app and support network.

It makes sense for budget-conscious owners of big homes who mainly want the dock to do the emptying.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a long self-empty interval.
products.skipIf: You want a proven app and long-term brand support.

products.name: Q10 Pro Self-Emptying Laser Navigation Robot Vacuum
products.verdict: A stated 150 minutes per charge with laser mapping. Fewer recharge stops across a big floor.
products.description:
This Q10 Pro model lists 150 minutes of runtime per charge, the longest single-charge figure in the guide, along with laser navigation and smart mapping. In a large home, runtime sets how many times the robot has to break off and recharge to finish a pass.

It lands sixth because it is a lesser-known brand and the rest of the spec sheet is more ordinary than the models above. 8000Pa suction and a self-emptying dock are solid, but there is little that differentiates it beyond the endurance figure.

Best for a large single-level home where one long run is better than several short ones.
products.idealFor: Big single-level homes that need fewer recharge stops.
products.skipIf: You want a major brand app and support.

products.name: Vyzzle Robot Vacuum and Mop E20
products.verdict: 8000Pa with carpet and hard floor modes in one combo machine. Newer brand, sensible spec sheet.
products.description:
The Vyzzle E20 combines 8000Pa suction with vacuum and mop functions and separate carpet and hard floor modes. For a large home with mixed flooring, one machine that adapts is simpler than running two.

It ranks below the established brands because it has less history behind it and fewer standout features than the roborock and eufy models above. In a big house, behavior across many rooms, including how it resumes after recharging, matters more than the spec line, and that is easier to trust from a proven platform.

It suits pet owners who want a combo machine from a newer name and are comfortable with that tradeoff.
products.idealFor: Pet owners with mixed floors who like a newer brand.
products.skipIf: You want the safest, most established platform.

products.name: ILIFE A30 Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: 10,000Pa max suction for under $200. The value pick when the budget is tight.
products.description:
The A30 Pro lists 10,000Pa maximum suction and combines vacuuming with mopping, all in the sub-$200 bracket. That number matches far pricier machines on paper, which makes it the clearest bargain for a big home on a tight budget.

It ends up last because the savings come from what is missing. There is no long-interval dock or premium mopping system to take work off your hands, so in a large home you carry more of the routine yourself.

Buy it if price is the main constraint and you are happy to empty and maintain it more often than the docked models.
pros: Vacuums and mops in one run
cons: More manual upkeep in a big house
products.idealFor: Tight budgets that still need strong suction numbers.
products.skipIf: You want a hands-off, self-maintaining setup.

whatMatters.detail: A home over about 2,500 square feet can need more than one battery charge for a full pass. Look for a stated runtime in minutes, not a vague claim like long battery life, and compare it with your floor area. Models that recharge and resume handle the gap, but they take longer overall.

A self-empty dock moves debris from the robot's small bin into a larger bag or bin. The rated interval, such as up to 7 to 9 weeks or 90 days, tells you how often you touch it. Check the listing for the exact figure, since dock capacity assumes typical, not heavy, dust loads.

A plain pad mop spreads whatever it picks up as it dirties. A roller mop or washing dock cleans the mop as it works, which matters across many rooms. If you have lots of hard flooring, look for a washing or self-cleaning mop system in the spec bullets.

Laser or mapped navigation lets the robot plan rows and resume after recharging. A multi-floor home needs saved maps for each level. Read the listing for map storage and multi-floor mapping before buying, because basic navigation can re-clean rooms and waste battery.
Mixed flooring needs a robot that raises or avoids mop pads on carpet and adjusts suction. Look for explicit carpet detection or separate carpet modes. Without them, a mopping robot can wet a rug.

faq.q: How much suction does a large home really need?
faq.a: Past about 8000Pa the gains are small for everyday dust. Runtime and a dock that empties itself matter more. Models like the eufy E25 at 20,000Pa pay off mainly with heavy pet hair or ground-in dirt.

faq.q: Can one robot vacuum cover a whole large house?
faq.a: Usually yes, if it can recharge and resume. A long-runtime model such as the Q10 Pro with 150 minutes per charge needs fewer stops. Without recharge-and-resume it will stop short on bigger floor plans.

faq.q: Does the roborock Q7 M5+ justify its price over the ILIFE A30 Pro?
faq.a: If you hate emptying the bin, yes. The dock is rated up to 7 to 9 weeks. The ILIFE has no comparable dock, so you manage the dustbin yourself, which gets tiring in a large home.

faq.q: Will a mopping robot damage my rugs?
faq.a: It can leave them damp if it does not detect carpet. Look for carpet modes or detection in the listing, such as on the eufy Omni C20 or Vyzzle E20, and keep rugs out of mopping zones in the app.

faq.q: How often should I replace the dock bag or empty the bin?
faq.a: Follow the dock's rated interval as an upper limit, not a target. Homes with pets fill bags faster. Check the bag when you notice weaker suction or a bulky smell, and keep spares of your model's bag.
In a big home it helps. Laser mapping builds a full layout and plans efficient rows, so it wastes less battery. Camera or basic navigation can also work but may re-clean areas.

finalTake: For most large homes the roborock Q7 M5+ is the right buy: 10,000Pa and a dock rated for up to 7 to 9 weeks of debris. If dirt is the bigger challenge, the eufy E25 brings 20,000Pa and a self-cleaning roller mop. Want hands-off on a budget? The MONSGA and its 90-day dock is the economical route. And if cost matters most, the ILIFE A30 Pro keeps strong suction numbers under $200.
